compensating.why: hop 3 builds the String from the whole buffer instead of the reported end
hop 4 reports at least the full length of the copies
hop 2 writes the first copy and then a separator in front of each further copy

ownership_reason: Only the gold writes the copies into the buffer and reports where they end; the facade, the count guard, the separator placement, the buffer allocation and the pass-through only hand on the String, the separator, the count and the buffer. Once the copies have been written over each other at index 0 and the end index is 0, the String built from the buffer is empty and no caller can recover the copies from it with a one-line change; no re-parameterisation avoids the omission (every call with a count of one or more reports 0). The convention of copying at the current end and then advancing it is the one of StrBuilder.append(char[]) (arraycopy at the end, then size += length) and ArrayUtils.addAll (second array placed at array1.length); the plain repeat overload and rightPad lay copies end to end, and their passing tests pin the result lengths and contents.
